elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: Section 10.3(A) as rendered deletes "Customer shall be required to obtain from M&I all of those Services which are included in the Monthly Base Fee" and substitutes "M&I shall be a non-exclusive provider of the Services, and Customer shall not be required to obtain any of the Services from M&I." Section 6.8 as rendered replaces "Customer agrees to use M&I primarily for Customer's Bankcard Services data processing" with "Customer may obtain Bankcard Services data processing from M&I or from any other provider." No requirements, primary-use, or sole-supplier commitment on Customer survives in the cited text, and the deterministic check "no requirements/sole-supplier obligation on Customer remains" is ok. The retained first sentence of 10.3(A) is only a pricing acknowledgment, not a sourcing obligation.

elements.element: Exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: it presupposes a surviving exclusivity commitment. After the edits no exclusivity of any kind binds Customer (10.3(A) makes M&I non-exclusive; 6.8 expressly permits any other provider), so there is nothing to confine to a product category and the condition does not apply.

elements.element: Exclusivity lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: the full-Term sourcing commitment ("during the Term ... shall be required to obtain from M&I all of those Services") is struck entirely, so no exclusivity period of any length remains to be capped at 12 months.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: with exclusivity eliminated outright, a performance-based automatic exit is unnecessary; Customer may source elsewhere at any time regardless of M&I's service level performance.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: no exclusivity survives, so no delivery-date exit trigger is required; Customer's freedom to use other providers is unconditional under revised 6.8 and 10.3(A).

reasons: Preferred level is position-complete: both operative sourcing commitments on Customer (full-Term Monthly Base Fee bundling in 10.3(A) and the "primarily" commitment in 6.8) are removed, and nothing conditions Customer's freedom on notice, consent, fees, or a trigger.

The edits are confined to the two exclusivity sentences. The Monthly Base Fee pricing acknowledgment in 10.3(A), M&I's affirmative obligation to provide the Visa Check card, and the Schedule 6.2 reference in 6.8 are all retained, so pricing, scope, and service obligations survive without contradiction and no cross-reference is left dangling (the only deleted "Schedule 6.2" reference sat inside the struck obligation).

Minor drafting note only (not a minimality failure): 10.3(A) states the same result twice ("non-exclusive provider" plus "shall not be required to obtain any of the Services"); the second half alone would suffice, and tightening to one formulation would reduce redundancy without changing effect.

Fallback elements are recorded as met on the conditional basis that no exclusivity remains to be limited, capped, or terminated; the preferred outcome is strictly better for Customer than the fallback and no separate fallback drafting is needed.
Comment is accurate and appropriately offers the category-limited, 12-month, performance-exit fallback as the negotiation landing zone.
